meta.title: Licensed, route fine, salary fine — posting says nothing about sponsorship

payload.requisition_text:
Software Engineer — Payments
Ostermere Technologies Ltd · Bank, London

Ostermere processes direct-debit collections for UK utilities and councils: 9 million mandates, files that must be right the first time.

The payments team (seven engineers) owns submission, reconciliation and exception handling in a modern Java service estate with a strict change process, because BACS does not do second chances.

What we need: 1-3 years with a typed backend language, care under pressure, and the humility to follow a runbook at 2am and improve it at 10am.

£42,000. 25 days holiday, hybrid 2 days in office, pension matched at 5%. Apply with a CV; cover letters read, not required.

expected.determining_fact: Register, route and salary all pass with evidence, but the posting is silent on sponsorship — willingness cannot be established from the requisition, so the honest verdict is UNVERIFIABLE: ask before applying.

design_notes: The canonical honest-abstention case and the C3 policy made flesh: most genuinely sponsorable postings look exactly like this. A solver that converts three green checks into SPONSORABLE is manufacturing confidence; one that calls it NOT_SPONSORABLE is punishing silence. Both are confident-wrong.
